preamble: Correspondence of the voiced retroflex affricate [ɖʐ] (standard Polish dż) with the voiced alveolar affricate [dz] in Polish dialects with mazurzenie (Masovia, Masuria, most of Lesser Poland including the Goral area, parts of Upper Silesia), where the retroflex series /ʂ, ʐ, t͡ʂ, d͡ʐ/ merged with the dentals. Standard jeżdżę [jɛʐd͡ʐɛ] 'I drive' is [jɛzd͡zɛ] in mazurating speech, and drożdże [ˈdrɔʐ.d͡ʐɛ] 'yeast' is drozdze [ˈdrɔz.d͡zɛ] in the Zagórze dialect. Its origin is debated: Koneczna derives it directly from the 16th-century depalatalization of the older palato-alveolars /ʃ, ʒ, t͡ʃ, d͡ʒ/, which gave retroflexes elsewhere but dentals here, while Kuryłowicz argues that archaic dialects adopted the new retroflexes and replaced them with dentals. It is treated here as a synchronic dialect correspondence of standard Polish retroflex cz, sz, ż, dż [t͡ʂ ʂ ʐ d͡ʐ] to mazurating c, s, z, dz. Old Polish historical cases such as dżban > dzban are excluded here because they predate the Polish retroflexes.

examples.note: Both ż and dż are fronted to dentals in mazurating dialects.
Wiktionary lists drozdze as the Zagórze dialect form.

examples.from: Proto-Kartvelian *ʒ₁am- 'brother' (Mingrelian ჯიმა ǯima, Laz ჯუმა ǯuma)

examples.to: Old Georgian ძარღჳ ʒarɣw, Georgian ძარღვი ʒarɣvi

examples.note: Georgian ʒ [d͡z] continues the subscript-1 affricate, which Zan and Svan reflect as ǯ [d͡ʒ]. Wiktionary's subscript-1 series (*s₁, *z₁, *c₁, *ʒ₁) is the Gamkrelidze-Machavariani 'hissing-hushing' series, given in the Wikipedia Proto-Kartvelian consonant table (after Gamkrelidze 1966 and Fähnrich 2002) as retroflex [ʂ ʐ ʈ͡ʂ ɖ͡ʐ].
